newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends lower as funds sell, meal mixed.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends lower as funds sell, meal mixed.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures closed lower on Friday amid fund selling while soymeal ended mixed with new crop up on weekend weather uncertainties, pit sources said.

Forecasts called for temperatures to warm this weekend with no substantial moisture expected in the central U.S. Midwest through the middle of next week. But some midday updates hinted at a chance for scattered showers.

"Latest short range guidance indicates a few light showers will occur over northern portions of the Midwest tonight (Friday) and in the south on Saturday," Weather Services Corp wrote in the midday update.
"Most of the activity will be under 0.25 inch with only spotty coverage," WSC said.
Below-normal rainfall during July is taking a visible toll on crops in Illinois, Missouri and Indiana and permanent yield losses are expected, agronomists in those areas said.
"I think there's not a question that the corn and bean crops are in a condition that would not be described as ideal," said University of Illinois agronomist Gary Pepper.
Soymeal ended $2.60 per ton higher to $2.40 lower with December up $1.40 at $216.60. Soyoil closed 0.38 to 0.24 cent per lb lower with December down 0.33 at 22.74 cents.

The National Oilseed Processors Association weekly crush report was neutral. NOPA early Friday said the U.S. soy crush during the week ended July 30 totalled 23.577 million bushels, within the range of expectations.
Prudential Securities was a featured seller of soyoil on the break, traders said, adding that volume was very thin.

On the day, Smith Barney bought 600 lots December soymeal, Merrill Lynch bought 400 December and 200 August and Cargill Investor Services sold 500 December, traders said. Refco Inc sold 500 October and 100 August.
In soyoil, Prudential Securities sold 500 December and bought 400 December. CIS bought 400 December and ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp sold 300 December.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 25,000 lots, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 28,761 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 25,000 lots, against Thursday's actual total of 32,350.
